attributes.body_ja:
「まい」は否定（ひてい）の意思（いし）を表（あらわ）す助動詞（じょどうし）で、肯定（こうてい）の意思（いし）を表（あらわ）す助動詞（じょどうし）である「う」や「よう」とは反対（はんたい）の役割（やくわり）を果（は）たします。「まい」は動詞（どうし）の原形（げんけい）に付（つ）いて使（つか）われます。また、これは少（すこ）し硬（かた）い表現（ひょうげん）とされています。

「まい」は、「(A) しないつもりだ」や「恐（おそ）らく (A) ではない」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。これは「〜ないだろう」をより短（みじか）くした表現（ひょうげん）だとも考（かんが）えられます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「まい」が「する」や「来（く）る」と一緒（いっしょ）に使（つか）われる場合（ばあい）、「しまい」「すまい」「きまい」「こまい」のように、「まい」が動詞（どうし）の連用形（れんようけい）に繋（つな）がることがよくあります。ただし、「するまい」や「来（く）るまい」のような形（かたち）もよく使（つか）われています。
attributes.body:
The auxiliary verb まい is used in Japanese to express negative volition. This means that in many ways, it is the opposite of う and よう, which are the auxiliary verbs that express positive volition. まい connects to the base form of verbs, and is considered slightly formal.

まい may be translated as 'won't (A)', 'to intend not to (A)', or 'probably not (A)'. It can be considered as a condensed way of expressing ～ないだろう.

Caution

When appearing with する or 来（く）る, it is also common to see まい connected to the conjunctive form as しまい, すまい, きまい and こまい. However, the standard するまい and 来（く）るまい are also quite common structures.

attributes.body: Though these two phrases appear similar in form, both suggesting 'without doing', they differ in that ともなく・ともなしに is used figuratively to express that the action was performed, but in an absentminded manner, or ‘without even so much as the intention of doing (A), (B)’ e.g. 見るともなく見ていたら 'as I was absentmindedly looking...', whereas ないで literally means that action was not performed, e.g. 見ずにやる 'do without looking'.

attributes.body: まい and だろう are both used to express speculation, but they contrast in polarity. だろう indicates positive speculation or likelihood, as in 雨が降るだろう (It will probably rain), while まい expresses strong negative speculation or denial, as in 雨は降るまい (It probably won’t rain).

attributes.body: まい and the volitional form (〜よう) both express the speaker’s intent or decision, but in opposite directions. 〜よう indicates intention or willingness to do something, as in 行こう (Let’s go), while まい expresses a strong negative intention or refusal, as in 行くまい (I will not go).3

attributes.body: まい was previously introduced with verbs as a condensed (and somewhat more formal) way of saying ないだろう. This is that same まい used with the negative form じゃない following nouns, and combined with し to list reasons, resulting in a phrase meaning 'You're/It's not (A), so...' , e.g. 子どもじゃあるまいし  ('You're not a child, so...').
